proposedchanges.title: AP Compared Trump Administration Statements on Iran Over Time
proposedchanges.description_short: AP Compared Trump Administration Statements on Iran Over Time
proposedchanges.description_long: The Associated Press assembled public statements from Donald Trump and senior officials about Iran from the June 2025 strikes through the start of the 2026 war. On June 24, 2025, Trump said Iran’s nuclear sites were “completely destroyed.” Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and the White House repeated that description the next day. Before U.S.-Israeli strikes began on February 28, 2026, officials again called Iran’s nuclear program an urgent threat. AP also traced Trump’s comments on regime change. After years of criticizing such missions, Trump wrote in June 2025 that regime change could be warranted and, after the 2026 strikes, urged Iranians to take over their government. These statements marked a change in public emphasis from declaring damage to nuclear sites to warning about nuclear ambitions and discussing political change. The chronology records public language and does not show whether each statement led to a new military order or formal policy change. It offers a dated comparison of how the administration explained its Iran policy.

evidencebasis: The packet and latest descriptions identify statements about Iran’s nuclear sites, renewed warnings, and regime change. They do not establish a formal benchmark or delayed oversight finding. The AP URL remains in source_urls.
notes: The revised title and long description report the statement chronology without claiming an oversight effect.

proposedchanges.title: AP Traced Changing Trump Administration Statements on Iran
proposedchanges.description_short: AP Traced Changing Trump Administration Statements on Iran
proposedchanges.description_long: An Associated Press report published March 2, 2026, traced Donald Trump and his administration’s public statements about Iran’s nuclear program and possible military action. After strikes the previous summer, officials said the attacks had destroyed or set back the program. In the lead-up to later U.S.-Israeli strikes, Trump and administration officials issued more urgent warnings about Iran’s nuclear ambitions. AP also recounted Trump’s January threats of military action amid protests in Iran, followed by his decision to step back after he said he had been assured Tehran had stopped killing protesters and had not carried out a planned execution. The report compared these statements over time; it did not independently assess Iran’s nuclear capabilities or document how allied governments responded. The sequence covers both the nuclear rationale and protest-related threats. It shows how public explanations and proposed actions shifted, but does not establish that U.S. military objectives formally changed or that allied plans were disrupted.

evidencebasis: The latest long description lists the summer strike claims, later nuclear warnings, January threats, and Trump’s subsequent decision to step back. It says the AP report does not document allied planning effects. The AP URL remains in source_urls.
notes: The revised title and long description focus on the documented statement sequence and avoid claims about allied planning.
